title: 320: Hundred Years' War: The Black Prince (Part 3)

sentences.en: Nigel tethered pommers to a thornbush and then turned his attention to the injured man.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔把波默斯拴在荆棘丛上，随后将注意力转向了那个受伤的男人。

sentences.en: He was a mere stripling, with the delicate features of a woman and a pair of great violet-blue eyes, which looked up presently with a puzzled stare into Nigel's face.
sentences.zh: 他不过是个毛头小子，长着一张女性般精致的脸庞，还有一双硕大的紫蓝色眼睛，此刻正困惑地盯着奈杰尔的脸看。

sentences.en: Who are you?
sentences.zh: 你是谁？

sentences.en: he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问道。

sentences.en: Ah, yes, I call you to mind.
sentences.zh: 啊，没错，我想起来了。

sentences.en: You are the young Englishman who chased me on the great yellow horse.
sentences.zh: 你就是那个骑着大黄马追赶我的年轻英国人。

sentences.en: By our lady of Roccomador, whose vernacle is round my neck.
sentences.zh: 以罗卡马杜尔圣母之名起誓，她的圣像正挂在我的颈间。

sentences.en: I could not have believed that any horse could have kept to the heels of Charlemagne so long,
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信，竟然有马能紧跟查理曼这么久。

sentences.en: but I will wager you a hundred crowns, Englishman, that I lead you over a five-mile course.
sentences.zh: 但我敢和你打赌一百个金冠，英国人，我能带你在五英里的赛道上跑赢你。

sentences.en: Nay, said Nigel.
sentences.zh: “不，”奈杰尔说。

sentences.en: Sounds like a horse.
sentences.zh: 听起来像匹马。

sentences.en: Nay, said Nigel.
sentences.zh: “不，”奈杰尔说。

sentences.en: We will wait until you can back a horse.
sentences.zh: 我们要等到你能骑马为止。

sentences.en: Eh, we talk of racing it.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们在谈论赛马的事。

sentences.en: I am Nigel of Tilford, of the family of Loring, a squire by rank and the son of a knight.
sentences.zh: 我是蒂尔福德的奈杰尔，出身洛林家族，是一名侍从，也是一位骑士的儿子。

sentences.en: How are you called, young sir?
sentences.zh: 年轻人，你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: I am also a squire by rank and the son of a knight.
sentences.zh: 我也是一名侍从，也是一位骑士的儿子。

sentences.en: I am Raoul de la Roche-Pierre de Bras, whose father writes himself Lord of Grosbois, a free vavasour of the noble Count of Toulouse, with the right of Fossa and of Firca,
sentences.zh: 我是拉乌尔·德·拉·罗什-皮埃尔·德·布拉斯，我父亲自称格罗布瓦领主，是图卢兹尊贵伯爵麾下的一名自由封臣，拥有福萨和菲尔卡的司法权。

sentences.en: the high justice, the middle and the low.
sentences.zh: 高等司法权、中等司法权和低等司法权。

sentences.en: He sat up and rubbed his eyes.
sentences.zh: 他坐起身，揉了揉眼睛。

sentences.en: Englishman, you have saved my life as I would have saved yours had I seen such yelping dogs set upon a man of blood and of coat armour.
sentences.zh: 英国人，你救了我的命，若是我见到这群吠叫的走狗围攻一位出身高贵、身披甲胄的绅士，我也定会救他。

sentences.en: But now I am yours.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我属于你了。

sentences.en: And what is your sweet will?
sentences.zh: 那么，你有什么吩咐？

sentences.en: When you are fit to ride, you will come back with me to my people.
sentences.zh: 等你身体好转能骑马了，就随我回我的族人那里去。

sentences.en: Alas, I had feared that you would say so.
sentences.zh: 唉，我早料到你会这么说。

sentences.en: Had I taken you, Nigel, that is your name, is it not?
sentences.zh: 如果是我抓住了你，奈杰尔——这是你的名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Had I taken you, I would not have acted thus.
sentences.zh: 如果是我抓住了你，我绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland, that is Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's novel.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆·赫兰德，那可是阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士的小说。

sentences.en: Beautifully written, as usual.
sentences.zh: 写得真漂亮，一如既往。

sentences.en: Sir Nigel, both beautifully written and I think it's fair to say remarkably read.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔爵士，不仅写得漂亮，我认为读得也相当出色。

sentences.en: Beautifully read, yeah.
sentences.zh: 读得真好，没错。

sentences.en: Those readings from Sir Nigel, with which we're introducing our epic sweep through the Hundred Years' War,
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔爵士的那些读物，我们正用它们来引出我们对百年战争的宏大叙事，

sentences.en: Arthur Conan Doyle always thought they were better than the Sherlock Holmes books.
sentences.zh: 阿瑟·柯南·道尔一直认为它们比《福尔摩斯探案集》更出色。

sentences.en: And he was gutted, wasn't he, that people paid so much attention to Holmes and not enough to Nigel.
sentences.zh: 他当时一定很沮丧吧，毕竟人们把太多关注给了福尔摩斯，而忽略了奈杰尔。

sentences.en: And actually, although we are, it's fair to say we're not reading them, well, I'm not reading them with an entirely straight face.
sentences.zh: 说实话，虽然我们确实在读，但公平地说，我们读的时候，嗯，至少我读的时候，很难完全严肃起来。

sentences.en: They do capture the sort of sense of the Hundred Years' War as this great gallant chivalric.
sentences.zh: 它们确实捕捉到了那种将百年战争视为一场伟大、英勇且充满骑士精神的战争的氛围。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, as a bit of a game.
sentences.zh: 是的，算是一种游戏吧。

sentences.en: I mean, it probably didn't seem that way to the blind king of Perhemia when he was riding the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当佩赫米亚的盲王骑马走错方向时，他可能并不这么觉得。

sentences.en: Well, no, but it did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实没有，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: It did because he died a chivalric death.
sentences.zh: 之所以这么说，是因为他死得很有骑士风度。

sentences.en: Yes, that's fair.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很公平。

sentences.en: And the codes of chivalry are still very important in this period.
sentences.zh: 而且骑士准则在这一时期仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's interesting about the Hundred Years' War and makes it significant is the way that it starts to mutate those codes,
sentences.zh: 百年战争之所以有趣且意义重大，原因之一就在于它开始改变这些准则，

sentences.en: both because they are used very, very powerfully by both French and English kings and knights,
sentences.zh: 这既是因为法英两国的国王和骑士们都在极力利用这些准则，

sentences.en: but also because of the impact of the way that the English fight, which starts to diminish the rank and the status of the traditional knightly classes.
sentences.zh: 也是因为英军作战方式的影响，这种方式开始削弱传统骑士阶层的地位和等级。

sentences.en: Well, we ended last time by talking about the Battle of Cressy, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们上次结束时谈到了克雷西战役，对吧？

sentences.en: And the longbow and military technology.
sentences.zh: 还有长弓和军事技术。

sentences.en: You know, there are arguments that it's even the first modern battle because it's won by projectiles rather than by people fighting hand to hand.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有人认为这甚至是第一场现代战争，因为它是靠远程武器取胜，而不是靠近身肉搏。

sentences.en: But on the other thing about the Sir Nigel spirit of gallantry and chivalry, so listeners who heard the first two episodes will recall that we went through the origins of the war,
sentences.zh: 但关于奈杰尔爵士那种英勇和骑士精神，听过前两期节目的听众应该还记得，我们梳理了战争的起源，

sentences.en: Edward III launching this sort of preemptive strike almost on France, the great superpower of Europe,
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世对欧洲超级大国法国发动了近乎先发制人的打击，

sentences.en: and then winning these tremendous battles at Sluice and then at Taken Calais and Cressy.
sentences.zh: 随后在斯勒伊斯、加来和克雷西赢得了辉煌的胜利。

sentences.en: But all of that happens against the backdrop of this looming catastrophe with which we ended last time, which is the advent of the Black Death.
sentences.zh: 但所有这一切都发生在我们上次提到的那场迫在眉睫的灾难背景之下，那就是黑死病的降临。

sentences.en: So he had this amazing moment.
sentences.zh: 所以他曾有过那样一段辉煌的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This ship pulls into Messina, dead men at the oars, the description in Barbara Tuckman's book, A Distant Mirror.
sentences.zh: 正如芭芭拉·塔克曼在《远方之镜》一书中所描述的那样，那艘船驶入墨西拿港时，划桨的人都已经死了。

sentences.en: So everything that we're going to talk about from now on happens against the backdrop,
sentences.zh: 所以我们接下来要谈的一切，都是在这样一个背景下发生的，

sentences.en: arguably one of the most devastating backdrops in Western history, which is the advent of the plague.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是西方历史上最具破坏性的背景之一，即瘟疫的降临。

sentences.en: Well, actually, Sir Nigel, Conan Doyle's novel, opens with a brilliant account of the Black Death coming.
sentences.zh: 其实，柯南·道尔的小说《奈杰尔爵士》开篇就精彩地描述了黑死病的到来。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't remember much of what happens in Sir Nigel, but I do remember that opening.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不记得《奈杰尔爵士》里的太多情节，但我确实记得那个开场。

sentences.en: But the strange thing is you were saying in our last episode that the Black Death changes everything.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，你在上一期节目中说黑死病改变了一切。

sentences.en: And obviously on one level it does.
sentences.zh: 从某种层面上看，显然确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, up to a third of Europe's population gets wiped out.
sentences.zh: 我是说，欧洲三分之一的人口被消灭了。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a catastrophe on an enormous, enormous scale.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一场规模极其巨大的灾难。

sentences.en: But at the same time, actually, in the context of the war, it doesn't change very much.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在战争的背景下，它其实并没有改变太多。

sentences.en: That's the strange thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: It brings a halt to the fighting.
sentences.zh: 它让战斗陷入了停滞。

sentences.en: So we said that the Black Death arrives in Europe a month or so after the capture of Calais.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，黑死病是在加来被攻陷一个月左右后传到欧洲的。

sentences.en: It's reached France that winter.
sentences.zh: 那个冬天它就传到了法国。

sentences.en: It reaches England the following summer.
sentences.zh: 第二年夏天它传到了英国。

sentences.en: People in Scotland are laughing.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人还在那儿笑呢。

sentences.en: Ha ha, the English are all dying of it.
sentences.zh: 哈哈，英国人都快死光了。

sentences.en: And then it reaches Scotland and they will start dying of it as well.
sentences.zh: 结果它随后传到了苏格兰，他们也开始死于瘟疫。

sentences.en: So it does definitely put a pause on the conflict, but it certainly doesn't bring it to an end.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实让冲突暂停了，但绝对没有让战争结束。

sentences.en: And it certainly doesn't stop Edward's war aims because essentially the Black Death serves to pause the conflict.
sentences.zh: 而且它也绝对没有阻止爱德华的战争目标，因为从本质上讲，黑死病只是让冲突暂停了而已。

sentences.en: And Edward is in pole position because he has the upper hand militarily.
sentences.zh: 爱德华占据了优势地位，因为他在军事上更胜一筹。

sentences.en: But crucially, he also has the upper hand in terms of prestige.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，他在声望上也占据了上风。

sentences.en: So this is a world, you know, I mean, beautifully rendered by Conan Doyle and articulated in your reading, in which these codes do matter.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个世界，你知道，我的意思是，柯南·道尔将其渲染得非常精彩，而你在朗读中也表达得淋漓尽致，在这个世界里，这些准则确实很重要。

sentences.en: And the person who can kind of lay claim to them and to present himself as the model of those codes is actually, you know, that's a strong position to be in.
sentences.zh: 而能够宣称自己拥有这些准则，并将其作为这些准则的典范展示出来的人，实际上，你知道，那是一个非常有利的地位。

sentences.en: So listeners who heard the first two episodes will know that Edward did not go to war because he wanted to be king of France.
sentences.zh: 所以听过前两集节目的听众会知道，爱德华发动战争并不是因为他想成为法国国王。

sentences.en: That ends up being a kind of justification or tactic during his war.
sentences.zh: 那最终成了他战争期间的一种辩解或策略。

sentences.en: But he goes to war really to protect his own realm from what he sees as inevitable French attack.
sentences.zh: 但他发动战争实际上是为了保护自己的领土，免受他所认为的不可避免的法国进攻。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And his claim to the French throne is basically a kind of bargain encounter.
sentences.zh: 而他对法国王位的要求基本上是一种讨价还价的手段。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Post-Cressy, does he still see it that way or does he now think, okay, I can actually do this.
sentences.zh: 克雷西战役之后，他还是那样看吗？还是他现在觉得，好吧，我真的可以做到。

sentences.en: I could become king of France.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为法国国王。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a strategic genius.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一位战略天才。

sentences.en: He understands the way that power works and armies work.
sentences.zh: 他了解权力的运作方式和军队的运作方式。

sentences.en: And he, I think, appreciates the fact that he has no real prospect of conquering the whole of France.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他很清楚自己实际上没有征服整个法国的希望。

sentences.en: His aim is to use his claim to the French crown to leverage as many possessions as he can get out of the French king.
sentences.zh: 他的目的是利用他对法国王位的要求，从法国国王那里尽可能多地争取领地。

sentences.en: And also, crucially, to get the French king to acknowledge that these possessions are sovereign.
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要的是，要让法国国王承认这些领地是主权领土。

sentences.en: In other words, Edward will no longer have to kind of pay homage to the French crown for these possessions.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，爱德华将不再需要因为这些领地而向法国王室效忠。

sentences.en: But obviously, he can't admit that because if he says that, then the whole scam fails.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他不能承认这一点，因为如果他说了，整个骗局就失败了。

sentences.en: So he has to project himself as a potential king of France.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须把自己塑造成一个潜在的法国国王。

sentences.en: And to do that, he has to present himself basically as the greatest king in Christendom because that is his ambition.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他必须把自己表现为基督教世界中最伟大的国王，因为这就是他的野心。

sentences.en: And he can do that because he is palpably a greater warrior and a kind of more glamorous, a more burnished figure than Philip VI,
sentences.zh: 他能做到这一点，因为他显然是一位更伟大的战士，比起腓力六世，他是一个更迷人、更光彩照人的人物，

sentences.en: who's left very diminished by his defeat at Cressy.
sentences.zh: 腓力六世在克雷西战役惨败后显得非常落魄。

sentences.en: And Edward's aim, which he triumphantly fulfills, oddly, you know, in the aftermath of Calais, when the Black Death is raging, is to establish himself as a new King Arthur,
sentences.zh: 爱德华的目标——他奇迹般地实现了——是在加来战役之后，当黑死病肆虐时，将自己确立为新的亚瑟王，

sentences.en: ruling over a new Camelot, even as his strategy, its long run effect will be to demolish the kind of the knightly ideals that he's articulated.
sentences.zh: 统治着一个新的卡美洛，尽管他的战略从长远来看会摧毁他所宣扬的那种骑士理想。

sentences.en: So that's the kind of the paradox of his reign.
sentences.zh: 这就是他统治时期的悖论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But I think there's absolutely a sense in the wake of Cressy and Calais that England and France, even while hostilities have been paused by the onset of the Black Death,
sentences.zh: 但我认为在克雷西和加来战役之后，绝对有一种感觉，即英格兰和法国，即使敌对行动因黑死病的爆发而暂停，

sentences.en: they are kind of competing for the upper ground of chivalric glory.
sentences.zh: 他们也在争夺骑士荣耀的制高点。

sentences.en: And so one of the things about this is that knights are the closest equivalent of sports stars that the Middle Ages have.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一点就是，骑士是中世纪最接近体育明星的存在。

sentences.en: These are figures with kind of international renown.
sentences.zh: 这些人拥有某种国际声誉。

sentences.en: And so their relative status does matter.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的相对地位确实很重要。

sentences.en: So the emblematic figure for the French is a man called Geoffrey de Charny, who, like so many of the great knights right the way through the Middle Ages, is he's actually,
sentences.zh: 法国人的代表人物是一个叫杰弗里·德·沙尔尼的人，他像中世纪所有伟大的骑士一样，实际上，

sentences.en: he's a third son of a relatively minor nobleman from Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 他是勃艮第一位相对较小的贵族的第三个儿子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But he rises to become the absolute sinisseur of French chivalry.
sentences.zh: 但他崛起成为了法国骑士精神的绝对典范。

sentences.en: And he does that because he's basically, you know, he's the Mbappé of tournaments.
sentences.zh: 他之所以能做到这一点，是因为他基本上，你知道，他是锦标赛里的姆巴佩。

sentences.en: He is superb.
sentences.zh: 他非常出色。

sentences.en: Well, not as good as Messi, is that your claim?
sentences.zh: 嗯，不如梅西好，这是你的主张吗？

sentences.en: That prince is Messi.
sentences.zh: 那位王子才是梅西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想也是。

sentences.en: We'll come to who might be the Messi.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再谈谁可能是梅西。

sentences.en: So he does everything that a chevalier should.
sentences.zh: 所以他做了所有骑士应该做的事。

sentences.en: He goes on a crusade.
sentences.zh: 他参加了十字军东征。

sentences.en: He writes tomes on points of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了关于骑士准则的巨著。

sentences.en: He articulates a sense that being a knight is the finest service that anyone can do to God outside of actually becoming a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 他表达了一种观点，即成为一名骑士是除了成为神职人员之外，一个人能为上帝做的最好的服务。

sentences.en: And brilliantly, he's the first known owner of the Turin Shroud, which is kind of distinctive quality.
sentences.zh: 而且非常精彩的是，他是已知的第一位都灵裹尸布拥有者，这是一种独特的品质。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 那真不错。

sentences.en: But the question then is, well, what practical use is this to France?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这对法国有什么实际用途呢？

sentences.en: It's great that you have this kind of model of chivalry, but does it actually help France militarily?
sentences.zh: 拥有这种骑士典范固然很好，但这在军事上真的能帮助法国吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Charny is aware of this.
sentences.zh: 沙尔尼也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: He's anxious about this.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And so he wants to do his bit for France.
sentences.zh: 所以他想为法国尽自己的一份力量。

sentences.en: And so late in 1349, after the kind of the worst of the Black Death has passed,
sentences.zh: 因此在1349年末，在黑死病最严重的时期过去之后，

sentences.en: he decides he's going to retake Calais because he appreciates that Calais is the great strategic fruit of Edward's Cressy campaign.
sentences.zh: 他决定夺回加来，因为他意识到加来是爱德华克雷西战役中最大的战略果实。

sentences.en: And he also appreciates that this is a massive ask because Calais is now exclusively inhabited by English.
sentences.zh: 他也意识到这是一个巨大的挑战，因为加来现在完全由英国人居住。

sentences.en: It has this massive, massive concentration of troops, the largest concentration of troops anywhere in Europe.
sentences.zh: 它拥有极其庞大的军队集结，是欧洲任何地方军队集结规模最大的地方。

sentences.en: And so the idea that you can ride up to it like Sir Lancelot and take it out is fantastical.
sentences.zh: 所以像兰斯洛特爵士那样骑马冲过去并将其拿下的想法是异想天开的。

sentences.en: And Charny recognizes that.
sentences.zh: 沙尔尼也认识到了这一点。

sentences.en: But he's not obliged by the codes of chivalry simply to launch a full-on charge.
sentences.zh: 但他并不受骑士准则的约束，非要发起全面冲锋。

sentences.en: You know, he can deploy tricks and schemes and reasons as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他也可以运用诡计、计划和理由。

sentences.en: I mean, that's perfectly legitimate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是完全合法的。

sentences.en: So what he does is he approaches an Italian mercenary who's in Calais, a guy called Almeric of Pavia, and offers him a big bribe.
sentences.zh: 所以他所做的是接触了一位在加来的意大利雇佣兵，一个叫帕维亚的阿尔梅里克的人，并给了他一大笔贿赂。

sentences.en: And Almeric pockets it and says, yeah, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 阿尔梅里克收下了钱，说，太棒了。

sentences.en: I'll let you and your band of French troops in.
sentences.zh: 我会让你和你的法国军队进去。

sentences.en: And Almeric then takes ship, crosses the channel, comes to Edward's court on Christmas Eve and tells him what's doing.
sentences.zh: 然后阿尔梅里克乘船横渡海峡，在平安夜来到爱德华的宫廷，告诉了他这件事。

sentences.en: But Edward, this is a massive Christmas present.
sentences.zh: 但爱德华，这可是一份巨大的圣诞礼物。

sentences.en: What fun.
sentences.zh: 多有趣啊。

sentences.en: So him, the Black Prince, all the lads, they all abandon their Christmas festivities, take ship to Calais.
sentences.zh: 所以他，黑太子，还有所有的小伙子们，他们都放弃了圣诞庆祝活动，乘船前往加来。

sentences.en: Poor old Charny has no idea that they've arrived there.
sentences.zh: 可怜的沙尔尼根本不知道他们已经到了那里。

sentences.en: He's very naive, I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以公平地说，他非常天真，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, he's a model of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是骑士精神的典范。

sentences.en: Almeric lets a kind of advance guard of the French in.
sentences.zh: 阿尔梅里克放了一支法国先遣队进来。

sentences.en: They raise the banner over the gateway, and then they get wiped out.
sentences.zh: 他们在门口升起旗帜，然后就被全歼了。

sentences.en: And Edward sounds the trumpets, and they all get captured.
sentences.zh: 爱德华吹响了号角，他们全都被俘虏了。

sentences.en: And Charny gets taken prisoner and goes to England.
sentences.zh: 沙尔尼被俘，并被带到了英国。

sentences.en: So it's all very embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是太尴尬了。

sentences.en: And Edward has triumphed.
sentences.zh: 而爱德华取得了胜利。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in France, Philip VI, he's on his way out.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在法国，腓力六世即将下台。

sentences.en: And he dies in August 1350.
sentences.zh: 他于1350年8月去世。

sentences.en: And he's succeeded by his son, John, who becomes John II.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子约翰继位，成为约翰二世。

sentences.en: Your listeners may remember that John I was the five-year-old baby.
sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得，约翰一世是个五岁的孩子。

sentences.en: Oh, gosh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，是啊。

sentences.en: Who ruled for five days or something.
sentences.zh: 统治了五天还是多久来着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And to be honest, John II is pretty much as useless as John I.
sentences.zh: 老实说，约翰二世和约翰一世一样没什么用。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: He's a terrible – so he looks like a king.
sentences.zh: 他是个糟糕的——他看起来倒像个国王。

sentences.en: He's got a beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着胡子。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, central casting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，就像选角导演选出来的一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But he's terrible.
sentences.zh: 但他很糟糕。

sentences.en: He's kind of very insecure.
sentences.zh: 他非常缺乏安全感。

sentences.en: He's very obstinate, and he's incredibly thick.
sentences.zh: 他非常固执，而且极其愚蠢。

sentences.en: And if he's given two options, he will invariably choose the worst option and then kind of cling to it absolutely obdurately.
sentences.zh: 如果给他两个选择，他总是会选最差的那个，然后死死地坚持到底。

sentences.en: Barbara Tuckman says of him that he could have served Machiavelli as the model for the anti-prince.
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉·塔奇曼评价他说，他本可以作为马基雅维利笔下“反君主”的原型。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: So he's a terrible king.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个糟糕的国王。

sentences.en: But because he looks like a king, he feels that he should have an order of chivalry that adequately reflects his desire to be, you know, the most Christian king.
sentences.zh: 但因为他看起来像个国王，他觉得他应该建立一个骑士团，以充分体现他想成为“最虔诚的国王”的愿望。

sentences.en: And fortunately for him, a year after he succeeded to the throne, so July 1351, Geoffrey de Charny comes back from England.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，在他继位一年后，也就是1351年7月，杰弗里·德·沙尔尼从英国回来了。

sentences.en: He's been ransomed.
sentences.zh: 他被赎回来了。

sentences.en: And he is the guy, obviously, to advise the French king on setting up an order of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 显然，他就是那个能为法国国王建立骑士团提供建议的人。

sentences.en: He's the perfect guy.
sentences.zh: 他是最完美的人选。

sentences.en: So Geoffrey de Charny kind of draws up a rulebook, and this new order is to be called the Order of the Star.
sentences.zh: 于是杰弗里·德·沙尔尼起草了一本规则手册，这个新骑士团被命名为星辰骑士团。

sentences.en: And it is enshrined in honor of God, of Our Lady, and for the heightening of chivalry and augmenting of honor.
sentences.zh: 它的宗旨是尊崇上帝、圣母，并弘扬骑士精神、增加荣誉。

sentences.en: Geoffrey de Charny writes a complete guidebook for it.
sentences.zh: 杰弗里·德·沙尔尼为此写了一本完整的指南。

sentences.en: But the measure of how much Geoffrey de Charny has been thinking about this and the reasons for English success is that although he is the great star of tournaments,
sentences.zh: 但从杰弗里·德·沙尔尼对这件事的思考程度以及对英国成功原因的分析来看，尽管他是锦标赛中的大明星，

sentences.en: what you have to do to win entry into the Order of the Star isn't success in tournaments, as had traditionally been the case with the chivalry orders, but success in battle.
sentences.zh: 但要赢得进入星辰骑士团的资格，靠的不是传统骑士团所看重的锦标赛表现，而是战场上的功绩。

sentences.en: So members have to come and report their deeds in battle to the king.
sentences.zh: 所以成员们必须亲自前来向国王汇报他们的战功。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when they're enrolled in the Order, they have to swear a solemn oath that they will never retreat from battle.
sentences.zh: 当他们加入骑士团时，必须庄严宣誓绝不从战场上撤退。

sentences.en: They will stand their ground at all times.
sentences.zh: 他们必须时刻坚守阵地。

sentences.en: So this is the real thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是动真格的。

sentences.en: This is the, you know, this is hardcore.
sentences.zh: 这是，你知道，这是硬核的。

sentences.en: This isn't flummering around with like garters for ladies and stuff.
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么给女士们戴吊袜带之类的花架子。

sentences.en: This is pretty gritty.
sentences.zh: 这相当残酷。

sentences.en: That is absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 那绝对没错。

sentences.en: And it's clearly an attempt to adapt to Geoffrey de Charny's understanding that, you know, basically not run away, which loads had done at Cressy.
sentences.zh: 这显然是试图适应杰弗里·德·沙尔尼的理解，即基本上不要逃跑，而这正是克雷西战役中那些人所做的。

sentences.en: So this is, this new order is proclaimed with kind of lots of trumpets and hurrahs and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个新骑士团是在一片号角声和欢呼声中宣布成立的。

sentences.en: But the problem is, I mean, it's a bit rubbish, really.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，说实话，它有点烂。

sentences.en: Oh no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: How disappointing for the French.
sentences.zh: 对法国人来说真是太令人失望了。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: You know, the French court is the traditionally the model of chivalry, but they have the first meeting on the 6th of January, 1352.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法国宫廷传统上是骑士精神的典范，但他们在1352年1月6日举行了第一次会议。

sentences.en: And basically not many people turn up.
sentences.zh: 基本上没几个人到场。

sentences.en: So very embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 所以非常尴尬。

sentences.en: And even more embarrassing is the fact that one of the knights who does turn up is a guy who is commanding one of the key castles next to Calais.
sentences.zh: 更尴尬的是，到场的骑士中有一位是指挥加来附近关键城堡之一的指挥官。

sentences.en: So one of the French held castles next to Calais.
sentences.zh: 也就是法国人控制的加来附近的城堡之一。

sentences.en: So he comes to this meeting and while he's away, the English move in and grab his castle.
sentences.zh: 他来参加会议，结果在他离开期间，英国人趁虚而入夺走了他的城堡。

sentences.en: So it's all, you know, mortifying.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，你知道，真是丢脸。

sentences.en: That's very funny.
sentences.zh: 那太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Makes me proud to be English, that does.
sentences.zh: 这让我为自己是英国人感到自豪。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: But Dominic, what should also completely make you proud to be English is the fact that one of the reasons why the Order of the Star seems a bit pallid is that it's nothing compared
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，同样让你为自己是英国人感到自豪的是，星辰骑士团之所以显得有点黯淡，是因为它根本无法与

sentences.en: to the blaze of another order of chivalry that's just been set up.
sentences.zh: 刚刚成立的另一个骑士团的光芒相比。

sentences.en: And that has been set up by Edward III in England.
sentences.zh: 那是爱德华三世在英国建立的。

sentences.en: And it's an order of chivalry that is still going strong to this day.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个至今依然活跃的骑士团。

sentences.en: The Order of the Garter.
sentences.zh: 嘉德骑士团。

sentences.en: You see, I feel bad now because I made a disobliging remark about messing around with garters.
sentences.zh: 你看，我现在感觉很糟糕，因为我之前说了关于摆弄吊袜带的刻薄话。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But of course, the Order of the Garter is the top order of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 但当然，嘉德骑士团是最高级别的骑士团。

sentences.en: Tom, if we play our cards right for this podcast, I mean, I don't think a historian has ever got the garter.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，如果我们在这个播客里表现得好，我的意思是，我不认为有历史学家获得过嘉德勋章。

sentences.en: It'd be great, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 那会很棒，不是吗？

sentences.en: Have they?
sentences.zh: 他们有吗？

sentences.en: Churchill got the garter or, you know, I think John Major has it.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔获得过嘉德勋章，或者，我知道约翰·梅杰有。

sentences.en: If John Major has the garter, you could reasonably aspire to that.
sentences.zh: 如果约翰·梅杰都有嘉德勋章，你完全可以有理由去争取它。

sentences.en: Surely we can get it, can't we?
sentences.zh: 我们肯定能拿到，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, the Order of the Garter has been founded by Edward III at the absolute height of the
sentences.zh: 所以，嘉德骑士团是由爱德华三世在

sentences.en: Black Death.
sentences.zh: 黑死病最严重的时候创立的。

sentences.en: So, St. George's Day, 1349.
sentences.zh: 也就是1349年的圣乔治日。

sentences.en: And Edward has been advised by his physicians to socially distance.
sentences.zh: 爱德华当时被他的医生建议进行社交隔离。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, Edward, however, is very much not the kind of guy, I think, who would have worn a mask.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，爱德华，无论如何，我认为他绝不是那种会戴口罩的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He's a partying in Downing Street kind of fellow, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是个会在唐宁街开派对的那种人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He very much is.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: And his response to this advice from his physicians to socially distance is to hold an absolutely massive tournament and invite everybody to it.
sentences.zh: 他对医生社交隔离建议的回应是举办一场规模宏大的锦标赛，并邀请所有人参加。

sentences.en: That's actually Novak Djokovic type behaviour.
sentences.zh: 那简直是诺瓦克·德约科维奇式的行为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, this is what's going on with, on St. George's Day, massive tournament, loads of ladies, loads of knights.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是圣乔治日发生的事情，大型锦标赛，大量的女士，大量的骑士。

sentences.en: And this is when he introduces the Order of the Garter.
sentences.zh: 也就是在这时，他引入了嘉德骑士团。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what this does absolutely brilliantly and much more effectively than the Order of the Star is to fuse the Arthurian with a massive celebration of military victory.
sentences.zh: 这比星辰骑士团做得更出色、更有效的地方在于，它将亚瑟王传说与军事胜利的盛大庆祝活动融合在了一起。

sentences.en: So, on the Arthurian level, the fact that it's held at Windsor is really significant because
sentences.zh: 所以，在亚瑟王传说的层面上，它在温莎举行这一事实非常重要，因为

sentences.en: Windsor is thought to have been founded by Arthur.
sentences.zh: 温莎被认为是亚瑟王建立的。

sentences.en: And I think I said in a previous episode that when Edward first starts ruling in his own name, one of the first things he does is go to Glastonbury and he then comes back and
sentences.zh: 我想我在上一集说过，当爱德华第一次开始以自己的名义统治时，他做的第一件事就是去格拉斯顿伯里，然后他回来并

sentences.en: he starts building Windsor.
sentences.zh: 开始建造温莎。

sentences.en: So, the heart of Windsor Castle now, where the royal family still live, is the portion of the castle built by Edward III, basically to look like Camelot.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在温莎城堡的核心区域，也就是王室成员居住的地方，就是爱德华三世建造的那部分，基本上是为了看起来像卡美洛。

sentences.en: So, it's a kind of Arthurian fantasy.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种亚瑟王式的幻想。

sentences.en: The tournament that he holds when he's meant to be socially distancing, it's absolutely modelled on the tournaments that Arthur holds.
sentences.zh: 他在本该进行社交隔离时举办的锦标赛，完全是模仿亚瑟王举办的锦标赛。

sentences.en: People praise and celebrate, say, Queen Philippa as a new Guinevere.
sentences.zh: 人们赞美并庆祝，比如，称菲利帕王后为新的桂妮薇儿。

sentences.en: And the whole scene is, it's all about spectacle, dazzle, illusion, suspense.
sentences.zh: 整个场景，全是关于奇观、炫目、幻觉和悬念。

sentences.en: It's brilliantly done.
sentences.zh: 做得非常出色。

sentences.en: But it's also about proclaiming military glory.
sentences.zh: 但它也是为了宣扬军事荣耀。

sentences.en: You mentioned the garter.
sentences.zh: 你提到了嘉德。

sentences.en: So, the motto,
sentences.zh: 所以，那句格言，

sentences.en: evil be to he who thinks it.
sentences.zh: 心怀邪念者受辱。

sentences.en: And the joke in 1066 and all that is, honey, your garter's fallen off.
sentences.zh: 在《1066和所有那一切》里的笑话是，亲爱的，你的吊袜带掉了。

sentences.en: So, the story that comes to be told is that there is a lady, some say the Countess of Salisbury
sentences.zh: 所以，后来流传的故事是，有一位女士，有人说是索尔兹伯里伯爵夫人，

sentences.en: and her garter drops off and Edward nobly hands it back to her and this is what he says.
sentences.zh: 她的吊袜带掉了，爱德华高贵地把它捡起来还给她，这就是他所说的话。

sentences.en: But this is a late story and it's much likelier that that motto is the motto that Edward was using on the Cressy campaign.
sentences.zh: 但这只是个后来的故事，更有可能的是，这句格言是爱德华在克雷西战役期间使用的格言。

sentences.en: So, everything that he was doing on the Cressy campaign was for the cause of legitimacy in God is basically the spin.
sentences.zh: 所以，他在克雷西战役中所做的一切都是为了上帝的合法性事业，这基本上就是宣传。

sentences.en: And the garter in the 14th century, much more than in the 15th century, is actually associated with military figures rather than with women.
sentences.zh: 而且在14世纪，嘉德勋章与军事人物的联系远比与女性的联系要紧密，这与15世纪不同。

sentences.en: And it's particularly associated with Edward's most formidable lieutenant, the Earl of Lancaster,
sentences.zh: 它特别与爱德华最强大的副手兰开斯特伯爵有关，

sentences.en: who shortly after becomes the Duke of Lancaster, who is very much the leading English commander.
sentences.zh: 他不久后成为了兰开斯特公爵，是英国主要的军事指挥官。

sentences.en: He's led four wars in Scotland, in Gascony.
sentences.zh: 他在苏格兰、加斯科涅领导过四场战争。

sentences.en: He was at Sluice.
sentences.zh: 他参加了斯勒伊斯海战。

sentences.en: He was at Calais.
sentences.zh: 他参加了加来之战。

sentences.en: And he is enrolled as the second knight of the order.
sentences.zh: 他被列为骑士团的第二位骑士。

sentences.en: And he is a guy who is particularly associated with a military garter.
sentences.zh: 他是一个特别与军事嘉德勋章联系在一起的人。

sentences.en: So, that's the likeliest explanation for it.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是最可能的解释。

sentences.en: So, he is enrolled in it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他被列入其中。

sentences.en: Edward is obviously, you know, he's presiding over it.
sentences.zh: 爱德华显然，你知道，他在主持这一切。

sentences.en: The Black Prince is enrolled in it.
sentences.zh: 黑太子也被列入其中。

sentences.en: 26 in all, most of whom participated in the Cressy campaign.
sentences.zh: 总共26人，其中大多数都参加了克雷西战役。

sentences.en: Among them, I'm proud to say Sir Thomas Holland.
sentences.zh: 其中，我很自豪地说，有托马斯·霍兰德爵士。

sentences.en: Sir Thomas Holland.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·霍兰德爵士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, that's great.
sentences.zh: 所以，那太棒了。

sentences.en: So, I wouldn't be the first Tom Holland to be enrolled in it.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会是第一个被列入其中的托马斯·霍兰德。

sentences.en: No, you wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 不，你不会是。

sentences.en: That's something.
sentences.zh: 那很有意义。

sentences.en: And also, the guy who, again, from childhood, was always my chivalric hero, who is, I think, the English equivalent to Geoffrey de Charny.
sentences.zh: 还有，那个从童年起就一直是我骑士精神英雄的人，我认为他是杰弗里·德·沙尔尼的英国版本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's a man called Sir John Shandos.
sentences.zh: 他叫约翰·尚多斯爵士。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, tell us about Sir John.
sentences.zh: 现在，给我们讲讲约翰爵士。

sentences.en: I know you love him.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很喜欢他。

sentences.en: Well, you should know about him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你应该了解他。

sentences.en: You've been reading Sir Nigel.
sentences.zh: 你一直在读《奈杰尔爵士》。

sentences.en: Sir Nigel becomes the squire to Sir John Shandos.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔爵士成为了约翰·尚多斯爵士的侍从。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And John Shandos is, again, like Geoffrey de Charny, he's a younger son who rises to become one of the great chivalric and military figures in England and, indeed, in Europe.
sentences.zh: 约翰·尚多斯和杰弗里·德·沙尔尼一样，也是个次子，后来崛起成为英国乃至欧洲伟大的骑士和军事人物之一。

sentences.en: And it's that fusion of the chivalric and the military that is the key to his success.
sentences.zh: 正是这种骑士精神与军事才能的融合，才是他成功的关键。

sentences.en: And he's the warrior who had, at Sluice, he'd landed and kind of reconnoitered the French fleet and reports back to Edward what it is, so kind of very brave.
sentences.zh: 他是一位战士，在斯勒伊斯海战中，他登陆并侦察了法国舰队，然后向爱德华汇报了情况，所以他非常勇敢。

sentences.en: He'd stood beside the Black Prince, Cressy.
sentences.zh: 他在克雷西战役中站在黑太子身边。

sentences.en: So Frassier describes him as a man who is wise and full of wiles.
sentences.zh: 所以弗鲁瓦萨尔形容他是一个睿智且充满计谋的人。

sentences.en: And he's also a man of great sophistication, charisma.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个非常有修养、有魅力的人。

sentences.en: He's very fond of music, very fond of dancing.
sentences.zh: 他非常热爱音乐，也非常热爱舞蹈。

sentences.en: I mean, he's absolutely a class act.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他绝对是一位风度翩翩的绅士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he comes to serve the Black Prince as his right-hand man.
sentences.zh: 他来到黑太子身边，担任他的得力助手。

sentences.en: He's both friend and military advisor.
sentences.zh: 他既是朋友，也是军事顾问。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince, he's not oversold, is he, Tom?
sentences.zh: 而黑太子，他并没有被过分吹捧，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Is he as dashing and as gallant as I remember from my childhood textbooks?
sentences.zh: 他是否像我童年教科书里描述的那样英勇潇洒？

sentences.en: So there's debate about how the Black Prince, Edward of Woodstock, comes to get this soubriquet, the Black Prince.
sentences.zh: 关于爱德华·伍德斯托克（即黑太子）是如何得到“黑太子”这个绰号的，人们一直有争议。

sentences.en: Some say it's because of his armour, which might be possible.
sentences.zh: 有人说是因为他的盔甲，这倒是有可能。

sentences.en: Others say that it's because of his reputation in France, which is a dark one.
sentences.zh: 也有人说是因为他在法国的名声，那是一个阴暗的名声。

sentences.en: He is a hard, hard man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常冷酷、非常强硬的人。

sentences.en: But that kind of hardness isn't necessarily to his disrepute.
sentences.zh: 但那种强硬并不一定意味着他名声扫地。

sentences.en: Yeah, we haven't come here to slag off the Black Prince, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们来这儿可不是为了诋毁黑太子的，汤姆。

sentences.en: And if you told me that would happen in this podcast, I would never agree to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉我这期播客会变成那样，我绝不会同意录制的。

sentences.en: Dominic, wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: Because, again, chivalry in the 14th century, just as it perfectly entitles you to employ kind of Odyssean schemes and wheezes,
sentences.zh: 因为，再说一次，14世纪的骑士精神，就像它完全允许你使用奥德修斯式的计谋和诡计一样，

sentences.en: it doesn't prohibit you from essentially committing what today we would describe as war crimes.
sentences.zh: 它并不禁止你实施在今天会被描述为战争罪行的行为。

sentences.en: Okay, that's good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这倒不错。

sentences.en: So the Black Prince, he's still very young at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以，当时的黑太子还非常年轻。

sentences.en: He's kind of not yet in his 20s.
sentences.zh: 他还没到20岁。

sentences.en: He is celebrated across Europe already as the flower of chivalry, the young 16-year-old at Cressy who had won his spurs.
sentences.zh: 他已经在全欧洲被誉为骑士精神的典范，那个在克雷西战役中赢得荣誉的16岁少年。

sentences.en: But he also has a reputation for being a hard man.
sentences.zh: 但他也有一个冷酷之人的名声。

sentences.en: So by the time that the Order of the Garter is in Italy, he's already the most famous knight in Christendom.
sentences.zh: 所以当嘉德勋章在意大利出现时，他已经是基督教世界最著名的骑士了。

sentences.en: And this has a polarizing effect in the way that spectators to the Hundred Years' War understand the relative status of England and France.
sentences.zh: 这在百年战争的旁观者眼中产生了一种两极分化的影响，让他们重新审视英格兰和法国的相对地位。

sentences.en: So England, this minnow, has really started to kind of bulk up.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰，这个小虾米，确实开始变得强大起来了。

sentences.en: You know, as I keep saying, that matters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如我一直说的，这很重要。

sentences.en: And it matters as well, of course, that compared to Edward, John II rapidly comes to seem a complete loser.
sentences.zh: 当然，与爱德华相比，约翰二世很快就显得像个彻头彻尾的失败者，这一点也很重要。

sentences.en: Edward's genius is for keeping his nobility close to him, making them his allies, making them his friends, band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 爱德华的天才之处在于他能让贵族们紧随其后，使他们成为盟友，成为朋友，成为兄弟连。

sentences.en: That's what the Order of the Garter is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是嘉德勋章的意义所在。

sentences.en: John has a genius for alienating his nobility.
sentences.zh: 而约翰的天才之处在于他总能疏远自己的贵族。

sentences.en: So the Constable of France had been taken prisoner during the Cressy campaign.
sentences.zh: 法国王室统帅在克雷西战役期间被俘虏了。

sentences.en: He gets ransomed, comes back, John immediately executes him.
sentences.zh: 他被赎回后刚回来，约翰就立即处决了他。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是啊。

sentences.en: And the reason that he does this is because he's become very Edward II and wants to appoint one of his favourites as Constable.
sentences.zh: 他这么做的原因是他变得非常像爱德华二世，想要任命他的一位宠臣担任统帅。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A near relative of his called Charles, Charles d'Espagne, Charles of Spain.
sentences.zh: 他的一位近亲，名叫查理，即西班牙的查理。

sentences.en: And, you know, this, just as the nobility in the reign of Edward II had resented these displays of favouritism, so now in France they resent John's displays of favouritism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如爱德华二世统治时期的贵族曾对这种偏袒行为感到不满一样，现在的法国贵族也对约翰的偏袒行为感到不满。

sentences.en: And what makes this all the more dangerous is that Edward III is not John's only rival for the French throne.
sentences.zh: 而让这一切变得更加危险的是，爱德华三世并不是约翰争夺法国王位的唯一对手。

sentences.en: Yeah, I felt the story was getting insufficiently complicated, Tom, and we needed more contenders.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我感觉故事变得不够复杂了，汤姆，我们需要更多的竞争者。

sentences.en: There is a third rival.
sentences.zh: 还有第三个竞争对手。

sentences.en: Now, again, Dominic, you may remember that I flagged up.
sentences.zh: 现在，多米尼克，你可能还记得我提到过。

sentences.en: Oh, God, you did.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪，你确实提过。

sentences.en: Do you remember?
sentences.zh: 你还记得吗？

sentences.en: I flagged up the fact that there were these three contenders for the French throne.
sentences.zh: 我强调过有三个争夺法国王位的竞争者。

sentences.en: There was Edward III, there was Philip of Valois, and there was a third Philip, Philip of Everot.
sentences.zh: 一个是爱德华三世，一个是瓦卢瓦的腓力，还有一个是第三个腓力，埃夫勒的腓力。

sentences.en: And he gets married off to Joan, who was the four-year-old girl, so direct descendant of the Capetians.
sentences.zh: 他娶了琼，那个四岁的小女孩，卡佩王朝的直系后裔。

sentences.en: And Joan and Philip of Everot had married, and I said, the problem for the Valois will be if Joan then has a son.
sentences.zh: 琼和埃夫勒的腓力结婚了，我说过，瓦卢瓦家族的问题在于如果琼生了个儿子。

sentences.en: Don't tell me she did.
sentences.zh: 别告诉我她生了。

sentences.en: And Joan does have a son.
sentences.zh: 琼确实生了个儿子。

sentences.en: And this guy is also called Charles.
sentences.zh: 这家伙也叫查理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Charles de Navarre.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦拉的查理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Charles of Navarre.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦拉的查理。

sentences.en: He's very kind of...
sentences.zh: 他非常……

sentences.en: Well, you've never seen The Simpsons, have you?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你从来没看过《辛普森一家》，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I can see your notes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我能看到你的笔记。

sentences.en: You've just written the words, Mr. Burns.
sentences.zh: 你刚才写下了“伯恩斯先生”这几个字。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you probably know what Mr. Burns looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以你大概知道伯恩斯先生长什么样。

sentences.en: He's like the caretaker or something, is he?
sentences.zh: 他是看门人还是什么的，是吗？

sentences.en: Is he something of that elk?
sentences.zh: 他是那种类型的人吗？

sentences.en: No, he's the evil guy.
sentences.zh: 不，他是那个邪恶的角色。

sentences.en: He's the evil capitalist who owns the nuclear power station.
sentences.zh: 他是那个拥有核电站的邪恶资本家。

sentences.en: Well, I've never seen The Simpsons.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我从没看过《辛普森一家》。

sentences.en: If you look at the kind of portraits of Charles of Navarre, he looks slight.
sentences.zh: 如果你看纳瓦拉的查理的画像，他看起来很瘦弱。

sentences.en: He looks vulpine.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像狐狸一样狡猾。

sentences.en: He has kind of big, glistening eyes.
sentences.zh: 他有一双大而闪烁的眼睛。

sentences.en: He's a schemer.
sentences.zh: 他是个阴谋家。

sentences.en: He's a backstabber.
sentences.zh: 他是个背后捅刀子的人。

sentences.en: He's utterly unscrupulous.
sentences.zh: 他完全没有道德底线。

sentences.en: And the measure of how bad he is, he's actually called Charles the Bad.
sentences.zh: 衡量他有多坏的标准是，他实际上被称为“恶人查理”。

sentences.en: That was your name?
sentences.zh: 那是你的名字？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, sorry, name.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，抱歉，名字。

sentences.en: It's his nickname.
sentences.zh: 那是他的绰号。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And basically, he's so bad that all he does is go around plotting and scheming.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他坏到极点，整天只知道密谋和算计。

sentences.en: And it's unclear whether he wanted to become king of France or whether he just, you know, he's just doing it for the bants, whether he's doing it for the fun.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他是想成为法国国王，还是仅仅为了好玩，为了恶作剧。

sentences.en: He's kind of a Iago figure.
sentences.zh: 他有点像伊阿古那样的人物。

sentences.en: But basically, if there's a possibility to stir up trouble, he will take it.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，只要有机会制造麻烦，他就会抓住。

sentences.en: And so he has a younger brother who he commissions to murder the constable.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个弟弟，他指使弟弟去谋杀统帅。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 噢，是啊。

sentences.en: Charles de Spagna, who behaves very, very badly, lets himself down, you know, grovels, begs for mercy.
sentences.zh: 西班牙的查理，他表现得非常非常糟糕，丢尽了脸面，你知道，卑躬屈膝，乞求怜悯。

sentences.en: But no, he's exterminated.
sentences.zh: 但没用，他被除掉了。

sentences.en: And so by doing this, Charles the Bad wins the support of all the nobility who had resented the constable.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，恶人查理赢得了所有对统帅不满的贵族的支持。

sentences.en: John II promptly confiscates all Charles the Bad's lands in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 约翰二世立即没收了恶人查理在诺曼底的所有土地。

sentences.en: Charles enters into negotiations with the English.
sentences.zh: 查理开始与英格兰人进行谈判。

sentences.en: John II backs down.
sentences.zh: 约翰二世退缩了。

sentences.en: There's going to be a test, by the way, for listeners at the end of this.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，听众们在最后会有一个测试。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Basically, it's very, very easy to keep track of because essentially, if you think that you know who Charles the Bad is backing in the Hundred Years' War, you've got it wrong
sentences.zh: 基本上，这非常容易追踪，因为如果你认为你知道恶人查理在百年战争中支持谁，那你就错了，

sentences.en: because he will have changed sides.
sentences.zh: 因为他会再次倒戈。

sentences.en: He's constantly changing sides.
sentences.zh: 他一直在不断地更换阵营。

sentences.en: And so this is kind of creating further chaos in France that the stability of the monarchy is now becoming severely rocked.
sentences.zh: 这在法国造成了进一步的混乱，君主制的稳定性现在正受到严重动摇。

sentences.en: And John, thick though he is, understands this.
sentences.zh: 而约翰，尽管他很迟钝，但也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: He appreciates that things are really bad for him.
sentences.zh: 他明白自己的处境非常糟糕。

sentences.en: He really needs a treaty to try and sort Charles the Bad out, to try and put his rule on firmer foundations.
sentences.zh: 他确实需要一份条约来试图解决恶人查理的问题，试图让他的统治基础更加稳固。

sentences.en: And so because the Pope in Avignon is very much under the thumb of the French king, he's able to kind of basically push the papacy to try and really work towards creating a peace
sentences.zh: 由于阿维尼翁的教皇在很大程度上受制于法国国王，他能够基本上推动教廷努力促成英法之间的和平

sentences.en: treaty between England and France.
sentences.zh: 条约。

sentences.en: And Edward is very tempted by it.
sentences.zh: 爱德华对此非常动心。

sentences.en: But in the end, he turns it down, partly because he doesn't trust the Pope, because he thinks
sentences.zh: 但最终他拒绝了，部分原因是他不信任教皇，因为他认为教皇基本上是法国人，

sentences.en: the Pope is basically French, but also because Charles the Bad inevitably switches sides again,
sentences.zh: 但也因为恶人查理不可避免地再次倒戈，

sentences.en: stabs John in the back, and promises to join the English with an army in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 在背后捅了约翰一刀，并承诺带着一支军队在诺曼底加入英军。

sentences.en: And so this is in 1355.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在1355年。

sentences.en: So Edward thinks, well, this is too good an opportunity to miss.
sentences.zh: 爱德华认为，这是一个不容错过的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: So he draws up plans for a triple invasion.
sentences.zh: 于是他制定了三路入侵计划。

sentences.en: He is going to cross to Calais.
sentences.zh: 他将渡海前往加来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Duke of Lancaster is going to cross to Normandy and meet Charles the Bad.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特公爵将渡海前往诺曼底，与恶人查理会合。

sentences.en: The Black Prince is going to head to Gascony.
sentences.zh: 黑太子将前往加斯科涅。

sentences.en: So they draw up all these plans.
sentences.zh: 所以他们制定了所有这些计划。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They're ready to go when inevitably Charles the Bad switches sides again.
sentences.zh: 他们准备出发时，恶人查理不可避免地再次倒戈了。

sentences.en: Oh my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And moves back, starts backing, you know, gets reconciled to John.
sentences.zh: 他又转回去了，开始支持，你知道，与约翰和解了。

sentences.en: And he goes to the Louvre and he swears before John II that he had done nothing against the king that a loyal vassal might not properly do.
sentences.zh: 他去了卢浮宫，在约翰二世面前发誓，他从未做过任何忠诚的封臣不该做的事来对抗国王。

sentences.en: I think Charles the Bad is coming out of this pretty badly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得恶人查理在这件事中表现得相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Or well, depending on your view.
sentences.zh: 或者说，取决于你的看法。

sentences.en: Well, he's bad.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他就是个坏人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, he's bad through and through.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，他从头到脚都是个坏蛋。

sentences.en: And so this is a problem because obviously now it's no good for Normandy because the Duke of Lancaster won't have a kind of open port that Charles the Bad would have provided.
sentences.zh: 这成了一个问题，因为显然现在对诺曼底来说没好处了，因为兰开斯特公爵将无法获得恶人查理本应提供的开放港口。

sentences.en: Edward decides that he's not going to go to Calais.
sentences.zh: 爱德华决定不去加来了。

sentences.en: But the Black Prince, you know, he wants to have a crack at the French.
sentences.zh: 但黑太子，你知道，他想去教训一下法国人。

sentences.en: He wants to have another go.
sentences.zh: 他想再试一次。

sentences.en: So he goes anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以他还是去了。

sentences.en: So the 9th of September, 1355, he sets sail from Plymouth.
sentences.zh: 1355年9月9日，他从普利茅斯起航。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: And he's got a large expeditionary force and he heads off for Gascony and a series of campaigns that will make him perhaps the most famous knight in English history.
sentences.zh: 他率领着一支庞大的远征军前往加斯科涅，开启了一系列让他成为英国历史上最著名骑士的战役。

sentences.en: Oh, splendid.
sentences.zh: 噢，太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, let's find out what happens after the break.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们在休息后看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: See you in a minute.
sentences.zh: 一会儿见。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: We ended, as we always like to, on a cliffhanger, which was the Black Prince sailing from Plymouth
sentences.zh: 我们像往常一样，以悬念结尾，那就是黑太子于1355年9月9日从普利茅斯起航前往加斯科涅，

sentences.en: for Gascony on the 9th of September, 1355, bound, as Tom told us, for a series of campaigns that would enshrine him.
sentences.zh: 正如汤姆告诉我们的，他将开启一系列让他名垂青史的战役。

sentences.en: I think, Tom, not merely is the greatest knight in English history, but is the greatest knight of all time in European history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为他不仅是英国历史上最伟大的骑士，而且是欧洲历史上最伟大的骑士。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So, Tom, he arrives in Bordeaux, 20th of September, 1355.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，他于1355年9月20日抵达波尔多。

sentences.en: He's got 2,220 men, and he's also got your friend, Sir John Chandos, guest star of Sir
sentences.zh: 他有2220名士兵，还有你的朋友，约翰·钱多斯爵士，奈杰尔爵士的客串明星。

sentences.en: Nigel.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's there.
sentences.zh: 他也在那儿。

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the moment the Black Prince arrives, he's not hanging around.
sentences.zh: 好吧，黑太子一到，就没闲着。

sentences.en: He decides that he's going to go looting and pillaging across the south of France.
sentences.zh: 他决定去法国南部进行掠夺和劫掠。

sentences.en: This is the chevauché, the kind of English knights on tour.
sentences.zh: 这就是“骑兵劫掠”，也就是英国骑士们的巡回演出。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they're like kind of, you know, football hooligans, leaving trail of chaos.
sentences.zh: 他们就像足球流氓一样，留下一路混乱。

sentences.en: And because John and his lieutenants are worried about the English landing in northern France, they haven't come south to confront the Black Prince.
sentences.zh: 由于约翰和他的副官们担心英军在法国北部登陆，他们没有南下对抗黑太子。

sentences.en: So basically, the south is relatively undefended.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，南部地区几乎没有防御。

sentences.en: Black Prince is able to recruit maybe 4,000 or 5,000 Gascon troops.
sentences.zh: 黑太子大约能征召到四五千名加斯科尼士兵。

sentences.en: So he's got quite a large force.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有一支相当庞大的军队。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince moves at a terrifying speed, takes the French completely by surprise.
sentences.zh: 黑太子以惊人的速度推进，让法国人完全措手不及。

sentences.en: He's able to ford rivers that have never been forded before, and strikes deep into lands that haven't seen the English for decades, for many, many generations.
sentences.zh: 他能渡过从未有人渡过的河流，并深入到几十年来、甚至几代人都未曾见过英国人的土地上。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, these are lands that are incredibly rich.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些土地极其富饶。

sentences.en: They fully recovered from the Albigensian wars, you know, that we talked about in a previous episode.
sentences.zh: 它们已经从我们上一集提到的阿尔比十字军战争中完全恢复过来了。

sentences.en: So Froissat, the great chronicler, describes them as being one of the fattest lands in the world.
sentences.zh: 伟大的编年史家弗鲁瓦萨尔将这些地方描述为世界上最肥沃的土地之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is a place of great cities, enormously prosperous.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一个大城市林立、极其繁荣的地方。

sentences.en: The English arrive outside Carcassonne, and a true English style.
sentences.zh: 英国人抵达卡尔卡松城外，展现出真正的英式风格。

sentences.en: One of them describes it as being even better than York.
sentences.zh: 其中一人形容那里甚至比约克还要好。

sentences.en: Even better.
sentences.zh: 甚至更好。

sentences.en: Even better than York.
sentences.zh: 比约克还要好。

sentences.en: The highest praise you can think to give it.
sentences.zh: 这是你能想到的最高赞美了。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince advances almost to the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 黑太子一路推进，几乎到达了地中海。

sentences.en: And then by the end of November, he's back in Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 到了十一月底，他回到了阿基坦。

sentences.en: And everyone who's gone with him comes back enormously rich.
sentences.zh: 所有随他出征的人回来时都变得极其富有。

sentences.en: It's said that a thousand wagons piled high with loot.
sentences.zh: 据说有一千辆马车装满了战利品。

sentences.en: There's loads of prisoners who can be ransomed.
sentences.zh: 还有大量的俘虏可以用来索要赎金。

sentences.en: It's been great fun.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: They've destroyed 500 villages.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了500个村庄。

sentences.en: They've burned down a dozen towns.
sentences.zh: 他们烧毁了十几座城镇。

sentences.en: So, Tom, I know we're a patriotic podcast, but I should interject at this point and say, so this is all being fought on French soil.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我知道我们是一个爱国播客，但我得插一句，这一切都是在法国领土上进行的战争。

sentences.en: And for ordinary people, the Hundred Years' War is just a terrible, terrible business.
sentences.zh: 对于普通百姓来说，百年战争简直是一场可怕至极的灾难。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: And most of the chroniclers don't really dwell on that.
sentences.zh: 大多数编年史家并没有过多关注这一点。

sentences.en: But some of them do.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些人提到了。

sentences.en: And in Duke was Frassar will, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如弗鲁瓦萨尔公爵。

sentences.en: You know, he will say these people were innocent, and they're completely innocent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他会说这些人是无辜的，他们完全是无辜的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's part of the brutality of the chivalric code that they don't really count.
sentences.zh: 这是骑士准则中残酷的一部分，即他们根本不算什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Peasant lives don't matter.
sentences.zh: 农民的生命无关紧要。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, you'll maybe say this is a silly comparison.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可能会觉得这个比较很愚蠢。

sentences.en: But the combination of plague and extreme violence being visited on sort of unwitting peasant communities.
sentences.zh: 但瘟疫与极端暴力同时降临在那些毫无防备的农民社区身上。

sentences.en: Is there a hint of the Thirty Years' War about this, would you say?
sentences.zh: 你会说这有一点三十年战争的影子吗？

sentences.en: Perhaps in the long run.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看或许有。

sentences.en: But at the moment, the Black Prince is very clearly playing a role both as the Prince of
sentences.zh: 但目前，黑太子非常明确地扮演着双重角色，既是威尔士亲王，

sentences.en: Wales, so the heir to the English throne, and as the Duke of Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 也就是英国王位的继承人，同时也是阿基坦公爵。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the sense of a war between England and France at this point is still pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 所以此时英法战争的性质依然非常明确。

sentences.en: So the kind of the confusion and chaos that you get in the Thirty Years' War, it hasn't yet manifested itself.
sentences.zh: 那种在三十年战争中出现的混乱和无序，目前还没有显现出来。

sentences.en: So the Prince of Wales is in command of this campaign.
sentences.zh: 威尔士亲王指挥着这场战役。

sentences.en: It's not kind of slipping his control.
sentences.zh: 局势并没有失控。

sentences.en: It's not anarchic.
sentences.zh: 这并非无政府状态。

sentences.en: It's sort of very focused.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常有针对性的行动。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so the scale of this chevauché, you know, he's penetrated hundreds of miles deep into
sentences.zh: 所以这次骑兵劫掠的规模，你知道，他深入法国领土数百英里。

sentences.en: French territory.
sentences.zh: 没有人能阻挡他。

sentences.en: No one has opposed him.
sentences.zh: 这对比法国人的自信心是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: And so it's a shattering blow to French self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，这依然是一次英国的胜利。

sentences.en: So in that sense, it's still, this is an English success.
sentences.zh: 因此，这不仅为黑太子，也为英国王室赢得了荣耀。

sentences.en: One therefore that redounds to the glory, not just of the Black Prince, but of the English crown as well.
sentences.zh: 反过来说，这对约翰国王的形象绝对是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: And conversely, it's absolutely terrible for the image of John.
sentences.zh: 有些法国领主开始认为，他真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And there are French lords who are starting to think, you know, he's awful.
sentences.zh: 诺曼底有个叫阿尔库伯爵的人，是一位非常有影响力的诺曼领主，他大喊道：以基督的血起誓，这个国王是个废物，是个糟糕的统治者。

sentences.en: So there's a guy in Normandy, the Count of Arcoe, a very significant Norman lord, who cries out, by the blood of Christ, this king is a worthless man and a bad ruler.
sentences.zh: 他说得没错。

sentences.en: He's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一个“恶人”查理在场，这让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, it doesn't help that you've got Charles the Bad being bad on the scene.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他来说是极好的利用机会。

sentences.en: So this is eminently exploitable by him.
sentences.zh: 关于“恶人”查理，他的基地是在纳瓦拉吗？

sentences.en: Just on Charles the Bad, his base is Navarre.
sentences.zh: 那是对的吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 不，他的基地实际上是在诺曼底。

sentences.en: No, his base is actually Normandy.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 他确实拥有纳瓦拉，但他在法国各地都有领地，而且在诺曼底势力尤为强大。

sentences.en: So he does have Navarre, but he has lands all over France and he's particularly strong in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 除了他那种小丑般的邪恶之外，他的行为背后一定有某种逻辑吧，他是在保护自己在诺曼底的领地吗？

sentences.en: And apart from his sort of pantomime badness, I mean, there must be some rationale behind his, is his thinking just protecting his own domain in kind of Normandy and...
sentences.zh: 是的，他想扩张自己的领地。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wants to expand his domain.
sentences.zh: 他想让自己成为法国的领军人物，或许在某个时候夺取王位。

sentences.en: He wants to make himself the leading man in France and perhaps at some point encompass the crown.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们并不确定。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他似乎基本上就是为了好玩而参与各种阴谋诡计。

sentences.en: I mean, he seems basically to have engaged in kind of schemes and plots in huge part just for the fun of it.
sentences.zh: 他身上有一种伊阿古式的特质。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a kind of Iago-esque quality to him.
sentences.zh: 但他在这方面非常、非常擅长。

sentences.en: But he's very, very good at it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不仅开始招募像阿尔库伯爵这样的诺曼骑士首领加入他的阵营。

sentences.en: So he, I mean, not only does he start recruiting people like the Count of Arco to his cause, so leading Norman knights.
sentences.zh: “恶人”查理还设法收买了王太子，令人恼火且典型的是，

sentences.en: Charles the Bad also manages to suborn the Dauphin, who infuriatingly and typically is
sentences.zh: 他也叫查理，他债台高筑，对他父亲非常怨恨，就像王太子们通常那样。

sentences.en: also called Charles Charles, who's very debt-written, very resentful of his father, as Dauphins tend to be.
sentences.zh: 基本上，“恶人”查理把王太子拉到了他那一边。

sentences.en: And basically, Charles the Bad gets the Dauphin on his side.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他正与阿尔库伯爵和其他几位贵族密谋夺取并谋杀国王。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, he is scheming with the Count of Arco and various other noblemen to seize and murder the king.
sentences.zh: 目前还不完全清楚王太子是否知情。

sentences.en: It's not entirely clear whether the Dauphin is privy to this.
sentences.zh: 他可能并不知情。

sentences.en: He probably isn't.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎确实参与了一个计划，至少要剥夺约翰的权力，如果不是要他的命的话。

sentences.en: But he does seem to have been complicit in a scheme to deprive John at the very least of his power, if not his life.
sentences.zh: 所以这是法国王室核心的一场危机。

sentences.en: So this is a crisis at the absolute heart of the French royal state.
sentences.zh: 这件事最终被约翰揭穿了。

sentences.en: And it duly gets uncovered by
sentences.zh: 1356年4月，他抵达了诺曼底首府鲁昂，当时王太子正在那里招待“恶人”查理、阿尔库伯爵以及其他所有阴谋者。

sentences.en: John.
sentences.zh: 约翰闯入，指控在场的所有人叛国，下令逮捕“恶人”查理，将其带往巴黎关押起来。

sentences.en: And in April 1356, he arrives in Rouen, the capital of Normandy, where the Dauphin is hosting
sentences.zh: 其他阴谋者被处决，包括阿尔库伯爵。

sentences.en: Charles the Bad, the Count of Arco, all the other conspirators.
sentences.zh: 他们的头颅被砍下，尸体被拖到绞刑架上，用铁链吊起来，头颅则插在长矛上。

sentences.en: John marches in, accuses everybody there of treachery, has Charles the Bad arrested, taken away to Paris, where he's put under lock and key.
sentences.zh: 这再次让约翰在法国贵族心目中的形象大打折扣。

sentences.en: The other conspirators are executed, including the Count of Arco.
sentences.zh: “恶人”查理也是这些受害者之一吗？

sentences.en: Their heads are chopped, chopped off, their bodies are dragged to gibbets, hung up in chains, their heads stuck on lances.
sentences.zh: 不，“恶人”查理被逮捕并带到了巴黎。

sentences.en: This, again, does nothing to improve John's image with the aristocracy in France.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰准备杀掉那些密谋反对他的低阶贵族，但他仍然不敢除掉“恶人”查理，因为那会做得太过火。

sentences.en: And Charles the Bad is one of these victims?
sentences.zh: 这非常有《权力的游戏》的感觉。

sentences.en: No, Charles the Bad has been arrested and taken to Paris.
sentences.zh: 我是说，挑拨父子关系、阴谋、密谋者。

sentences.en: So John is ready to kill the kind of the lower order and ability who've been conspiring against him, but he's still not ready to get rid
sentences.zh: 可以推测，其后果是“恶人”查理的人马（纳瓦拉家族）与法国王室之间彻底决裂。

sentences.en: of Charles the Bad because that would be a step too far.
sentences.zh: 法国王室是指什么？

sentences.en: So that's very Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 瓦卢瓦王朝。

sentences.en: I mean, turning the son against the father, the plot, the conspirators.
sentences.zh: 瓦卢瓦王朝，抱歉，是瓦卢瓦王朝。

sentences.en: And presumably the consequence of that is a complete rift between Charles the
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Bad's people, the House of Navarre, and the, what's the House of France?
sentences.zh: 所以纳瓦拉家族随后否认了对法国王室的忠诚。

sentences.en: The Valois.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是诺曼底的大玩家，这使诺曼底陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: The Valois, sorry, the Valois.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也意味着纳瓦拉家族现在与英国结盟，这为英国远征军打开了大门，1356年7月，

sentences.en: Well, exactly.
sentences.zh: 由兰开斯特公爵率领的军队如期在瑟堡登陆。

sentences.en: So the House of Navarre then repudiates its loyalty to the French crown.
sentences.zh: 几个月前被约翰处决的所有诺曼底贵族的兄弟和继承人都向爱德华三世效忠。

sentences.en: And because they are the big players in Normandy, that plunges Normandy into chaos.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特公爵，正如英国战争领袖通常所做的那样，在诺曼底进行了一场大规模的骑兵劫掠，显然没有针对他新盟友的财产，但非常针对王室财产，随后进入了布列塔尼。

sentences.en: And of course, it means that the House of Navarre is now in alliance with England, which opens the gates to an English expeditionary force, which in July 1356,
sentences.zh: 然后，在八月下旬，他向南前往加斯科尼。

sentences.en: duly lands at Cherbourg, led by the Duke of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 因为与此同时，当兰开斯特公爵在北方散布混乱时，黑太子也在南方耍弄他的手段。

sentences.en: And the brothers and the heirs of all the noblemen in Normandy who had been executed by John a few months before do homage to Edward III, pledge loyalty to him.
sentences.zh: 他正从加斯科尼向北前往卢瓦尔河。

sentences.en: And the Duke of Lancaster, as English war leaders tend to do, goes on an enormous chevauché across Normandy, obviously not targeting the properties of his
sentences.zh: 卢瓦尔河是那条标志着、你知道，将法国一分为二的大河。

sentences.en: new allies, but very much targeting royal properties, and then into Brittany.
sentences.zh: 所以目标是让这两支由兰开斯特公爵和黑太子分别率领的英国大军在卢瓦尔河会合，

sentences.en: And then towards later August, he heads southwards towards Gascony.
sentences.zh: 联手然后，你知道，尽情狂欢。

sentences.en: Because meanwhile, while the Duke of
sentences.zh: 这就是计划。

sentences.en: Lancaster is spreading chaos in the north, the Black Prince is up to his tricks in the south.
sentences.zh: 现在，显然对于约翰来说，这是终极危机。

sentences.en: And he is heading northwards from Gascony towards the Loire.
sentences.zh: 他知道他不能让这种情况发生。

sentences.en: The Loire is the kind of the great river that marks, you know, divides the two halves of France.
sentences.zh: 于是他发出征召令，据说他集结了法国所有的精英。

sentences.en: And so the aim is for these two great
sentences.zh: 这是一种夸张，因为有很多贵族并没有响应他的号召，因为他们对他怀有敌意。

sentences.en: English armies led respectively by the Duke of Lancaster and by the Black Prince to meet at the
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是集结了一支庞大的军队，这可能是14世纪法国见过的最庞大的军队。

sentences.en: Loire gang up and then just, you know, have all kinds of fun.
sentences.zh: 这支军队由国王亲自率领，为了显示信心，他带上了所有的王室珠宝。

sentences.en: So that's the plan.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每当有人在战前这样做时，你只会想，难道你从历史中什么都没学到吗？

sentences.en: Now, obviously for
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: John, this is the crisis to end all crises.
sentences.zh: 或者也许那些赢得战斗的人也带了他们的王室珠宝，只是编年史家从未记录下来。

sentences.en: He knows that he cannot allow this to happen.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so he sends out summons, he raises, it's said, all the flower of France.
sentences.zh: 从多米尼克的评论来看，不知道结果的听众可能已经对将要发生的事情有某种预感了。

sentences.en: That's an exaggeration because there are lots of noblemen who don't come to his cause because they're actively hostile to him.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，如果你不想知道结果，现在就别看了。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, he raises a large force, probably the largest force that is seen in France in the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，现在别看了。

sentences.en: And it's personally led by the king, who as a token of his confidence takes with him all his crown jewels.
sentences.zh: 他还带上了他的四个儿子，包括王太子查理，以及他最小的儿子，不出所料，也叫菲利普。

sentences.en: I mean, whenever anyone does that before a battle, you just think, well, have you learned nothing from history?
sentences.zh: 所以这让事情变得更加混乱了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 随行的领主、骑士和王子们。

sentences.en: Or maybe people who win battles also take their crown jewels, but the chroniclers just never record it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们的人数足以组成一场耀眼的展示。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 他们都带着自己的旗帜，在空中骄傲地飘扬。

sentences.en: From Dominic's comment, listeners who don't know the result may have some kind of presentiment of what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以这支军队在行进时场面极其壮观。

sentences.en: I should have said, if you don't want to know the result, look away now.
sentences.zh: 当然，所有旗帜中最伟大的一面是我们在克雷西战役背景下提到的“奥里弗拉姆”战旗，这是法国国王带入战场的圣旗。

sentences.en: Yeah, look away now.
sentences.zh: 而那位在国王身边将它带入战场的人，是法国最著名的骑士，杰弗里·德·沙尔尼。

sentences.en: He also takes with him all four of his sons, including the Dauphin, Charles, and his youngest son, who inevitably is called Philip.
sentences.zh: 哦，想必星之勋章的成员也倾巢出动了，是吗？

sentences.en: So just to make things even more confusing.
sentences.zh: 星之勋章的成员绝对是倾巢出动了。

sentences.en: The lords, the knights, the princes who accompany him.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们发誓绝不逃跑。

sentences.en: I mean, there are more than enough to make a dazzling display.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不能后退。

sentences.en: They're all carrying their penance, fluttering proudly in the air.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So it's a tremendous spectacle, this army as it moves.
sentences.zh: 所以这次大集结寄予了极高的期望，希望法国国王终于能够围困并歼灭一支英国军队。

sentences.en: And of course, the greatest of all the flags, the war banners, is the Oriflame that we mentioned in the context of Cressy, the sacred banner born into battle by the French king.
sentences.zh: 消息传来，黑太子正在接近卢瓦尔河。

sentences.en: And the man who carries it into battle by the side of the king is France's most famous knight,
sentences.zh: 当然，如果他们要向北与兰开斯特公爵会合，他们就必须跨过卢瓦尔河。

sentences.en: Geoffrey de Charny.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，南部地区几乎没有防御。

sentences.en: Oh, and presumably the Order of the Star is out in force for this, is it?
sentences.zh: 黑太子大约能征召到四五千名加斯科尼士兵。

sentences.en: The Order of the Star is absolutely out in force.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有一支相当庞大的军队。

sentences.en: And of course, they're pledged never to run away.
sentences.zh: 黑太子以惊人的速度推进，让法国人完全措手不及。

sentences.en: No, they can't go backwards.
sentences.zh: 他能渡过从未有人渡过的河流，并深入到几十年来、甚至几代人都未曾见过英国人的土地上。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些土地极其富饶。

sentences.en: So hopes are very, very high in this great gathering that at last, a French king will be able to corner an English army and wipe it out.
sentences.zh: 它们已经从我们上一集提到的阿尔比十字军战争中完全恢复过来了。

sentences.en: And the news is brought that the Black Prince is approaching the Loire.
sentences.zh: 伟大的编年史家弗鲁瓦萨尔将这些地方描述为世界上最肥沃的土地之一。

sentences.en: And of course, they have to cross the Loire if they're going to go northwards and meet with the Duke of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一个大城市林立、极其繁荣的地方。

sentences.en: So the Black Prince sends his most trusted lieutenant, Sir John Chandos, to lead an advance party to try and find a ford.
sentences.zh: 于是黑太子派他最信任的副官约翰·钱多斯爵士率领一支先遣队去寻找浅滩。

sentences.en: They reach what they think is going to be a ford, and they find it guarded by French troops.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了他们认为会是浅滩的地方，却发现那里有法军把守。

sentences.en: Sir John Chandos, because he's tremendously cool, beats them off easily.
sentences.zh: 约翰·钱多斯爵士因为极其冷静，轻松地击退了他们。

sentences.en: But he finds that the river is too swollen to cross.
sentences.zh: 但他发现河水涨得太高，无法渡过。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of rain.
sentences.zh: 雨下得很大。

sentences.en: The Loire is very, very swollen.
sentences.zh: 卢瓦尔河水涨得非常、非常厉害。

sentences.en: So the Black Prince and his army start to move along the south bank of the Loire, trying to find a crossing.
sentences.zh: 于是黑太子和他的军队开始沿着卢瓦尔河南岸行进，试图寻找渡口。

sentences.en: But as had happened on the Crecy campaign, all the bridges have been cut, and they can't find a way to get over the Loire.
sentences.zh: 但就像克雷西战役期间发生的那样，所有的桥梁都被切断了，他们找不到过卢瓦尔河的方法。

sentences.en: News then reaches him that the French king is approaching him with a massive army.
sentences.zh: 随后有消息传来，法国国王正率领一支庞大的军队向他逼近。

sentences.en: And the
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: Black Prince does not have enough men with him, really, to meet this huge army in battle.
sentences.zh: 黑太子手下的兵力实在不足以与这支大军交战。

sentences.en: He really, really needs to join up with the Duke of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 他真的、真的需要与兰开斯特公爵会合。

sentences.en: And so he is kind of, you know, sending scouts out, frantically trying to find the Duke of Lancaster's expedition.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直在派侦察兵，疯狂地试图找到兰开斯特公爵的远征军。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, on the 10th of
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在9月10日，

sentences.en: September, the French have reached Bloire, on the Loire, where a bridge has been held for them, and they cross it.
sentences.zh: 法军到达了卢瓦尔河畔的布卢瓦，那里有一座桥为他们保留着，他们便过了桥。

sentences.en: 11th of September, they're closing in on the Black Prince.
sentences.zh: 9月11日，他们正在逼近黑太子。

sentences.en: And the Black
sentences.zh: 而黑

sentences.en: Prince is informed that this vast French army is now 10 miles from him, and he still can't find the
sentences.zh: 太子获悉这支庞大的法军现在离他只有10英里远，而他仍然找不到

sentences.en: Duke of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特公爵。

sentences.en: And he learns on the same day that the reason for this is that just as he can't get to the northern bank of the Loire, so the Duke of Lancaster can't get to the southern bank.
sentences.zh: 同一天他得知，之所以会这样，是因为正如他无法到达卢瓦尔河北岸一样，兰开斯特公爵也无法到达南岸。

sentences.en: So essentially, they're separated.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，他们被隔开了。

sentences.en: So the Black Prince retreats towards the town of Poitiers, which is just south, southwards of where he'd been.
sentences.zh: 于是黑太子向普瓦捷镇撤退，该镇就在他之前所在位置的南边。

sentences.en: And he stops there to wait to see if Lancaster will be able to get across.
sentences.zh: 他在那里停下来，等待看看兰开斯特是否能过河。

sentences.en: And as he halts there, the French army passes him about 10 miles to the east, and then pivots westwards.
sentences.zh: 就在他停驻时，法军从他东面约10英里处经过，然后向西转向。

sentences.en: So essentially, the road from Poitiers back to
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，从普瓦捷回

sentences.en: Gascony is cut off.
sentences.zh: 加斯科涅的路被切断了。

sentences.en: Bad news for the Black Prince, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这对黑太子来说是个坏消息，汤姆。

sentences.en: So what's the Black Prince going to do?
sentences.zh: 那么黑太子打算怎么办呢？

sentences.en: He decides he has no choice, really, but to offer battle.
sentences.zh: 他决定除了决战别无选择。

sentences.en: And so rather than alert the French to this, he orders his troops to advance through a forest so that the French won't know that he's approaching.
sentences.zh: 为了不让法军察觉，他命令部队穿过一片森林，这样法军就不会知道他在靠近。

sentences.en: And on the 17th of September, a company of Gascon's emerge from this forest, emerge from the wood, and they stumble into the
sentences.zh: 9月17日，一支加斯科涅连队从这片森林中走出，从树林里出来，他们撞上了

sentences.en: French rear guard and they rout it.
sentences.zh: 法军的后卫部队并将其击溃。

sentences.en: But of course, it's now the king and all the French command know that the English are basically within striking distance.
sentences.zh: 但当然，现在国王和所有法军指挥官都知道英军基本上就在打击范围内了。

sentences.en: And there's no point in hiding in the wood anymore.
sentences.zh: 躲在树林里已经没有意义了。

sentences.en: So the 18th of September, the English emerge from the wood.
sentences.zh: 于是9月18日，英军从树林中走了出来。

sentences.en: And there's a hill.
sentences.zh: 那里有一座小山。

sentences.en: It's about five miles south of Poitiers, overlooking a village called Neu.
sentences.zh: 它在普瓦捷以南约五英里处，俯瞰着一个叫讷的村庄。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince and
sentences.zh: 黑太子和

sentences.en: Sir John Chandos occupy this, raise their banners, take possession of it.
sentences.zh: 约翰·钱多斯爵士占领了这里，竖起旗帜，占据了该地。

sentences.en: But their situation is very bad because they don't have any food and they don't have any water.
sentences.zh: 但他们的处境非常糟糕，因为他们没有食物，也没有水。

sentences.en: Plus, they're pretty shattered.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: I was going to say they've been marching for hundreds of miles.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，他们已经行军数百英里了。

sentences.en: And also through the effort of pulling their wagons through the woods has not been stressful.
sentences.zh: 而且拉着马车穿过树林的过程也并不轻松。

sentences.en: So at this point, the English and the French are staring at each other.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，英法两军正对峙着。

sentences.en: Ambassadors from the Pope step in and they're led by a cardinal, the Cardinal of Perigord.
sentences.zh: 教皇的使节介入了，由一位红衣主教——佩里戈尔红衣主教领导。

sentences.en: And he senses that the English situation is very, very weak.
sentences.zh: 他感觉到英军的处境非常、非常脆弱。

sentences.en: And so perhaps this is an opportunity to lean on the Black Prince and get him to accept terms that would then also be acceptable to the French king.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许是一个向黑太子施压，让他接受法王也能接受的条款的机会。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince's situation is so grim that basically he says he is willing to negotiate, but John isn't because he feels that he has the English absolutely captured.
sentences.zh: 黑太子的处境如此严峻，以至于他基本上表示愿意谈判，但约翰国王不愿，因为他觉得他已经彻底困住了英军。

sentences.en: This is his chance to finish the most once and for good.
sentences.zh: 这是他一劳永逸地解决问题的机会。

sentences.en: So the cardinal's mediation efforts fail and loads of his entourage then go off and join the French, which only confirms English suspicions of what kind
sentences.zh: 所以红衣主教的调解努力失败了，他的许多随从随后离开并加入了法军，这只会证实英军对这些

sentences.en: of papal ambassadors are up to.
sentences.zh: 教皇使节意图的怀疑。

sentences.en: And so basically it becomes pretty certain that the following day, which is the 19th of September, there is going to be a battle.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上可以确定，第二天，也就是9月19日，将会有一场战斗。

sentences.en: Unless, of course, by some miracle, the Prince of Wales, the Black Prince can pull off a kind of retreat, somehow get away from this position where he's been cornered.
sentences.zh: 除非威尔士亲王，也就是黑太子，能奇迹般地完成某种撤退，以某种方式从这个被围困的位置逃脱。

sentences.en: But obviously the intention of the French is to stop that.
sentences.zh: 但显然法军的意图是阻止这一点。

sentences.en: So they draw up their battle lines and as they invariably do, as they've done at Cressy, they do it in three lines, three battalions.
sentences.zh: 于是他们排开了阵势，正如他们一贯所做的那样，就像在克雷西战役中一样，他们排成了三线，即三个营。

sentences.en: So the first line is commanded by the Dauphin, but he's still very young.
sentences.zh: 第一线由王太子指挥，但他还很年轻。

sentences.en: John doesn't entirely trust him.
sentences.zh: 约翰国王并不完全信任他。

sentences.en: So he has at his right hand a Scotsman,
sentences.zh: 所以他身边有一位苏格兰人，

sentences.en: Lord of Douglas, who in obedience to the old alliance has come to France with a contingent of Scots knights and warriors.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯勋爵，他为了遵守古老的盟约，带着一支由苏格兰骑士和战士组成的队伍来到了法国。

sentences.en: So they're in the front line.
sentences.zh: 所以他们站在前线。

sentences.en: And because they are used to fighting the English, they suggest to the French that they dismount from their horses.
sentences.zh: 而且因为他们习惯了与英军作战，他们建议法军下马。

sentences.en: In other words, that they don't watch a kind of full-on cavalry charge because this would not be, you know, otherwise they risk a repeat of the Battle of Cressy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不要进行那种全力的骑兵冲锋，因为这不会……否则他们会冒着重演克雷西战役的风险。

sentences.en: And this is advice that John is prepared to accept.
sentences.zh: 这是约翰国王准备接受的建议。

sentences.en: The second line is commanded by the Duke of Orléans, brother of the king, and two of the Dauphin's younger brothers are there.
sentences.zh: 第二线由国王的兄弟奥尔良公爵指挥，王太子的两个弟弟也在那里。

sentences.en: And the third line, it's the king with Geoffrey de Charny and the Oriflame and his youngest son, Philip.
sentences.zh: 第三线是国王本人，带着杰弗里·德·沙尔尼、奥里弗拉姆战旗和他最小的儿子菲利普。

sentences.en: So that's their battle line.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的战斗阵型。

sentences.en: And then having drawn it up, there's actually a delay because suddenly they start to think, well, perhaps we shouldn't fight a battle.
sentences.zh: 排好阵势后，实际上出现了一段延迟，因为他们突然开始想，也许我们不应该打这一仗。

sentences.en: Perhaps we should just stay here and starve the English out.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该留在这里，把英军饿死。

sentences.en: That would be the obvious thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那才是显而易见该做的事。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Black Prince has decided that he is going to try and retreat.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，黑太子已经决定他要尝试撤退。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is an incredibly difficult manoeuvre because it requires moving slowly
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一个极其困难的机动，因为它需要缓慢地

sentences.en: backwards through the wood and not alerting the French, but it's impossible not to alert the
sentences.zh: 穿过树林向后移动，且不能惊动法军，但要做到不惊动

sentences.en: French.
sentences.zh: 法军是不可能的。

sentences.en: And so not all the French are on foot.
sentences.zh: 而且并非所有法军都在步行。

sentences.en: Some are still on horseback and they notice the retreat.
sentences.zh: 有些人还在马背上，他们注意到了撤退。

sentences.en: And they're so excited by this that they immediately launch a charge.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到非常兴奋，于是立即发起了冲锋。

sentences.en: So they go careering up the hill, wiped out by the English archers.
sentences.zh: 他们冲上山坡，结果被英国弓箭手消灭了。

sentences.en: When the first French line sees this, they think, oh, we better march to the rescue.
sentences.zh: 当第一线法军看到这一幕时，他们想，哦，我们最好去救援。

sentences.en: And so they start marching up the hill.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始向山上进军。

sentences.en: And so the battle is joined and the fight goes on for two hours, but the French can't break through the English lines.
sentences.zh: 战斗就这样打响了，战斗持续了两个小时，但法军无法突破英军的防线。

sentences.en: And after two hours fighting, the French line breaks.
sentences.zh: 经过两个小时的战斗，法军防线崩溃了。

sentences.en: The Dauphin has to be hurried away because obviously they don't want to risk him being captured.
sentences.zh: 王太子不得不被匆忙带走，因为显然他们不想冒让他被俘的风险。

sentences.en: As the first line starts moving away, the second line commanded by the Duke of Orléans thinks that the battle is loSt. And so he starts withdrawing.
sentences.zh: 当第一线开始撤离时，由奥尔良公爵指挥的第二线认为战斗已经失败，于是开始撤退。

sentences.en: And as he goes, he's taking two of the Dauphin's younger brothers with him.
sentences.zh: 他走的时候，还带走了王太子的两个弟弟。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of chaos of confusion and misunderstanding.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种混乱和误解的局面。

sentences.en: And John, the king in the third line sees this and is humiliated and ashamed and mortified and is absolutely determined to save French honor.
sentences.zh: 而身处第三线的约翰国王看到这一幕，感到屈辱、羞愧和痛苦，他绝对决心要挽回法国的荣誉。

sentences.en: And of course, as the head of the Order of the Star, there's no prospect that he can possibly retreat.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为星之勋章的领袖，他绝无可能撤退。

sentences.en: And so instead he advances.
sentences.zh: 所以他反而发起了进攻。

sentences.en: And by this point, he's absolutely in with a shout because the English archers have run out of arrows.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，他绝对有胜算，因为英国弓箭手的箭已经用完了。

sentences.en: They're tired.
sentences.zh: 他们累了。

sentences.en: And basically all the greatest knights in France are with the king, all the members of the Order of the Star.
sentences.zh: 基本上法国最伟大的骑士都在国王身边，所有星之勋章的成员都在。

sentences.en: And so
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: the fighting is incredibly desperate.
sentences.zh: 战斗极其惨烈。

sentences.en: But with the result of the battle still absolutely hanging in the balance, one of the English captains notices that there's an opportunity for a flanking maneuver.
sentences.zh: 但就在战斗结果悬而未决之际，一名英国队长注意到有一个侧翼包抄的机会。

sentences.en: So he takes his men, he breaks from the line, and he moves around and starts to attack the French and their rear.
sentences.zh: 于是他带着手下脱离了防线，绕过去开始攻击法军的后方。

sentences.en: And this generates a kind of sense of chaos and panic in the French army.
sentences.zh: 这在法军中引发了一种混乱和恐慌。

sentences.en: And at this point, the Black Prince and Chandos appreciate that this is the moment.
sentences.zh: 此时，黑太子和钱多斯意识到时机到了。

sentences.en: This is their opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的机会。

sentences.en: And so they order all their knights to get on their horses.
sentences.zh: 于是他们命令所有的骑士上马。

sentences.en: The horses have been kept back in reserve to get on their horses and again, to launch another kind of flanking maneuver on the other wing.
sentences.zh: 马匹一直被留在后方作为预备队，骑士们上马，再次在另一侧翼发起了某种侧翼包抄。

sentences.en: And the French end up surrounded and essentially those who don't flee are annihilated.
sentences.zh: 法军最终被包围，基本上那些没有逃跑的人都被歼灭了。

sentences.en: And Frassard describes the culmination of the battle.
sentences.zh: 弗鲁瓦萨尔描述了战斗的高潮。

sentences.en: So he says, the pursuit of the routed French went on as far as the walls of Poitiers, where there was a fearful slaughter of men and horses.
sentences.zh: 他说，对溃败法军的追击一直持续到普瓦捷城墙下，那里发生了人马的惨烈屠杀。

sentences.en: The inhabitants of Poitiers shut the gates and refused to let anyone in.
